content: If you suspect poisoning, contact a poison control center immediately. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. Laboratory tests, such as kidney function, complete blood count, blood sugar levels, and cultures, may be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during treatment. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Gemifloxacin is used to treat various bacterial infections and belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully regarding dosage and duration of treatment. Take this medication at least two hours before or three hours after consuming products that may interfere with its effectiveness, such as antacids, sucralfate, or supplements containing iron, zinc, magnesium, or aluminum. Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, or difficulty sleeping. However, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile infection, which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Gemifloxacin may cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it can sometimes be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare, severe allergic reaction. The risk of developing a rash is higher in individuals under 40 years of age, women (especially those on hormone replacement therapy), or when the medication is taken for more than seven days. Before using gemifloxacin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin), or any other substances. This medication may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk is higher if you have certain medical conditions, take other drugs that prolong the QT interval, or have low potassium or magnesium levels due to conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Gemifloxacin may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, particularly in individuals with diabetes. Monitor your blood sugar regularly and report any symptoms of high blood sugar (e.g., increased thirst or urination) or low blood sugar (e.g., sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet). Carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar, or use quick sources of sugar like candy, honey, or fruit juice if necessary. This medication may cause dizziness, and alcohol or marijuana can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcohol consumption. Additionally, gemifloxacin may increase sensitivity to sunlight. Live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, may not work effectively while using this medication. Children may be at greater risk for joint or tendon problems when taking gemifloxacin. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it passes into breast milk in small amounts. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
